Not very often. It depends how much I enjoyed the title the first time round, and if I care for replaying it again. For example, the recent SEGA promo as part of the MWNL contest was giving away a number of free games, including Condemned Criminal Origins and Binary Domain. I enjoyed both titles enough to complete them to the end, but I see them as too much of a 'been there, done that' to play them again. That could be because I've only clocked them so recently, but there's also nothing majorly stand out about them. I probably would never have bought them myself, and it's nice to try stuff you wouldn't otherwise, but the realistic truth is that I'll probably never play them again.

Now, let me take Half Life 2. Not specifically because I have an admiration for it, but because of the Synergy mod, which I've sunk 41 hours into. Add that to my actual play time for HL2 and its episodes (18 hours, although I remember HL2 on the original Xbox and having jams on The Orange Box on both PS3s and 360s), and I've spent probably over 100 hours in Half Life 2. And you know what? I'm sick of it. I can't load it up without saying lines word-for-word, and getting bored within half an hour.

Then there's games like Fallout New Vegas, which I've spent 75 hours in and have never completed fully. I know how it ends, and I know the differing plot paths (mostly, of course), but I still plan to pick up some mods and complete it someday.

So case-by-case basis for me personally, although not really that often.

I figure I have spent about $3,000 on ammo, much of which is still stockpiled, over the last six months. Basically, anytime I found an online deal that dropped the price per round to something to good to pass on, I'd buy a thousand rounds. I shoot 45APC, 9MM Luger, .380 and .556 Nato.

How long did it take you to break even (cost of equipment offset by savings on ammunition purchased), and how much does it cost you to produce each round? This assume you save your casings. Thanks all.
For those of you who load, what set up do you use, and what did it cost you?

I reload. But less for cost savings and more a hobby/prepping measure.

You can't put a price tag on Owning the means of production.

I keep my setup simple, flexible and portable. Cast bullets from scavenged car wheel weights and handheld molds, hand press that can fit easily in a backpack. Knowledge of improvised propellant/powder sources.

I might not save much when I go to the range, but I have peace of mind knowing I can continually replenish my personal ammo loadout while potentially on the move.

I also dabble in designing projectiles and sabots. Right now working on a custom sabot that could fire any size projectile up to .700 from a standard 12-gauge shotgun. Again, handy in an improvised pinch.

Me and a buddy reload sharing the costs. Been doing it about 2 years now. I think we broke even after about 6-9 months. We got a Dillon 550 and can make 9mm for about half the cost of factory. We both shoot 200+ rounds a weekend at the range so we do go through a lot.

We ended up with so much brass, I purchased a cement mixer to clean the brass. Doing 5,000 rounds at a time vs the 400 we were doing when we steel tumbled helped us a lot.

We use the brass we pick up, Tightgroup power, plastic coated 147 grain bullets (Google "black bullets"). I think we use 3.1 grains of powder.

We also reload 45APC, 10mm and am looking into reloading my favorite round 22tcm.

It took us about 3 months of reloading and learning before we really started to crank out a lot of rounds. It was also helpful that the local reloading shop we go to had a guy that had been reloading for almost 40 years and always has time to answer questions.
Thanks. One of my neighbors loads, and he is going to teach me. I can use his equipment for a while, but will have to eventually get my own. We go through a lot of rounds too.
